thread.post: 1/ Morning Money Brief, Oct 24: September CPI, cited Thursday, rose 3.7% y/y, above the 3.6% estimate. That feeds Fed rate choices that set savings yields and mortgage costs. Fed decides Wed Oct 28. If it signals more hikes, borrowing may stay pricier.

2/ Friday's data: AI and chip stocks fell hard. META -7.0%, AMD -8.1%, CRWV -10.1%. No cause confirmed. Why it matters: index funds and 401(k)s often hold these names. Watch GOOGL and MSFT earnings Oct 28. Weak results could keep tech volatile.

3/ Bitcoin is near $80,607, down 1.2% in 24h. Ethereum sits at $2,369. Why it matters: big coins are drifting, but small tokens like Irys (+50.6%) moved with no news found. If volume fades, those spikes can reverse fast. Not financial advice.

video.script: Your money moved this week, and most people missed why. Here's your Morning Money Brief for Saturday, October 24. First, inflation: September CPI rose 3.7 percent from a year earlier, above the 3.6 percent estimate. That feeds the Fed's rate decision on Wednesday, which affects savings yields and mortgage costs. Second, stocks: on Friday, AI and chip names sold off hard. Meta fell 7 percent, AMD 8.1 percent, and CoreWeave 10.1 percent. No cause was confirmed. If big tech earnings on October 28 disappoint, watch for more swings in index funds and 401(k)s. Third, crypto: Bitcoin sits near $80,607, down 1.2 percent in a day, while small coins spike with no clear news. Not financial advice. Follow for tomorrow's brief.
